prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats’ 2015 manifesto, “Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone,” sets out a five‑year plan to balance the budget fairly, boost opportunity, protect the NHS, and lead on the environment.

Key pledges
- Balance the budget by 2017/18 with a mix of spending restraint and fair tax measures on wealth, banks, big business and polluters; debt to fall as a share of GDP; no rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax.
- Cut taxes by raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500.
- Invest £8bn extra a year in the NHS by 2020 and give mental health equal status with physical health.
- Protect education funding from nursery to age 19 and require qualified teachers in every class.
- Enact five green laws to protect nature, clean air and water, cut waste, and reach net zero emissions by 2050.

Economy and jobs
- Long-term industrial strategy; double economy‑wide innovation spend; expand Catapult centres and the Green Investment Bank.
- Banking reform and more competition; support SMEs and alternative finance.
- Major infrastructure: HS2, extensive rail electrification, regional transport (e.g., Transport for the North), better South West links, East‑West Rail.
- Low‑carbon power: 50–100g CO2/kWh by 2030 with ~60% renewables; end unabated coal by 2025; scale CCS, storage and smart grids; expand community energy; cautious, strictly regulated shale with revenues for a Low‑carbon Transition Fund.
- Stay in and reform the EU; complete single market in digital/energy/services; pursue ambitious trade deals (protecting standards and the NHS); welcome high‑skill migrants and STEM students.

Family finances, welfare and work
- Extend free childcare towards 20 hours a week for all 2–4s and from 9 months for working parents; complete Tax‑Free Childcare and enhance support in Universal Credit.
- Roll out Universal Credit; devolve and improve back‑to‑work support; fair, targeted welfare with a temporary 1% uprating cap to 2017/18 (exempting disability/parental benefits).
- Promote flexible work, expand Shared Parental Leave, enforce the minimum wage, pay a Living Wage in central government, curb zero‑hours abuses.
- Pension “triple lock” in law; complete auto‑enrolment; protect pension freedoms.

Education and young people
- End child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025; expand early years quality and Pupil Premium.
- Slim national core curriculum (including PSHE, SRE, financial literacy); strengthen governance and Ofsted oversight of all school types.
- Double the number of businesses hiring apprentices; expand higher apprenticeships; improve FE and fair HE access; 16–21 bus discount.

Health and care
- Integrate health and social care funding; improve GP access; invest in community care.
- Mental health: national waiting time standards, broader access to talking therapies, transformed children’s services, 24/7 crisis care.
- Support carers (annual £250 bonus; care leave consultation); raise social care quality and workforce standards; strong public health (tobacco levy, minimum alcohol pricing, better food labelling).

Environment, transport and housing
- Five green laws: zero‑carbon by 2050; green transport (ULEVs, low‑emission zones); green buildings (efficiency targets, council tax incentive); zero‑waste (70% recycling); Nature Act (biodiversity, access, forestry).
- Build 300,000 homes/year including Garden Cities; planning led by robust Local Plans, brownfield first; expand affordable/intermediate housing (Rent to Own, shared ownership); stronger tenant protections; upgrade 4m homes by 2020.

Rights, justice and security
- Protect the Human Rights Act; Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; a Victims’ Bill of Rights; tackle VAWG.
- Rehabilitation focus with presumption against short prison terms; Portugal‑style diversion for drug possession; maintain tough action on trafficking and dealers.

Devolution and democracy
- Votes at 16; proportional representation (STV) for Westminster and local; elected Lords.
- Home Rule for Scotland/Wales/Northern Ireland; “Devolution on Demand” in England; party donation cap of £10,000.

Britain in the world
- Pro‑EU reform and engagement; in/out referendum only on future treaty change.
- Meet 0.7% aid; conflict prevention; Single Security Budget; scale down nuclear posture; climate leadership and global environmental protection.
